matchups.recap: Nori got absolutely obliterated this week, losing by 52.5 points like he forgot he was in a fantasy league and just randomly threw darts at a waiver wire board. That's not a loss, that's a goddamn public execution—your roster looked like a retirement home's shuffleboard team out there. Rob walked into this matchup and found a corpse waiting for him; honestly, he should've gotten bonus points just for showing up to compete against whatever dumpster fire you sent to the field.

Ben got absolutely fucking obliterated this week, losing by 67.5 points like he wandered into a fantasy football thunderdome with a wet noodle and a prayer. Scoring 56.4 is legitimately impressive in the worst possible way—that's the kind of performance that makes you wonder if Ben's entire roster collectively decided to take a personal day. Arben didn't just beat him; he put on a masterclass in fantasy dominance while Ben's team imploded harder than a house of cards in a hurricane. This wasn't a matchup, it was a mercy killing.

Veton got absolutely dicked down 117.3 to 99.2 this week, and honestly, that 18-point margin is being generous because it doesn't even capture how thoroughly Flamur's roster bent Veton over a barrel. Veton's team played like it was still hungover from the bye week, limping across the finish line while Flamur was out here scoring like he actually knew how to set a lineup. Maybe next week Veton will remember that putting active players on the field is kind of the whole point of this thing.

Rinor got absolutely obliterated by 45 points this week, which is genuinely impressive in how thoroughly he managed to shit the bed—that's not a close loss, that's a straight-up ass-kicking. Whatever lineup decisions he made were clearly made with his eyes closed and his brain in neutral, because there's no way you score 77.6 and accidentally do it that badly. Faton walked into this matchup like he was playing against a minor league squad and Rinor rolled over like a dead fish. This is the kind of loss that makes you question every life choice that led to your roster construction.

Adam got absolutely skull-fucked this week, losing by 20.6 points like he forgot half his roster existed on Sunday. 74.6 points is what you score when your "expert waiver wire pickups" are actually just guys who got injured in the second quarter. Ilir came in swinging with 95.2 and left Adam wondering if he should've just started his bench instead—it probably would've scored more.

Rilind got absolutely skull-fucked by a 10-point margin this week—and somehow that's still being generous considering the dumpster fire he's been running all season. Peter came in swinging with 97 points while Rilind limped across the finish line like a three-legged dog, and the gap between them was wider than Rilind's playoff hopes. This is what happens when your team management is about as competent as a screen door on a submarine.

matchups.preview: Two teams drowning in the same shit show, but Ben's about to go under first—because at least Rob has the excuse of bad luck; Ben's just been making catastrophically stupid roster decisions all season. This is basically a battle to see who can fumble away a winnable week harder, and honestly, both of these clowns are more than capable of finding new and creative ways to lose.

Nori's cruising at 4-2 while Veton's out here 0-fucking-6, which means this is less a matchup and more a mercy killing—except Nori's probably gonna find a way to start his third-string backup at QB and still somehow lose to the worst team in the league. Veton's been dead all season, but even a corpse gets a win eventually, and knowing Nori's track record of snatching defeat from the jaws of victory, this could be the week he donates one.

Arben's rolling in at 5-1 like he's actually competent, but we all know he's been riding the coattails of his draft luck and waiver-wire gambling—one bad week and this house of cards collapses faster than his decision-making in the fourth quarter. Faton's sneaking up at 4-2 with nothing to lose, and sometimes a team that's clawed their way back from mediocrity is exactly the kind of desperate energy that punches above their weight and exposes a fraud like this.

Muriqi's sitting pretty at 5-1, but let's be real—that record's held together with duct tape and prayer, carried entirely by whatever waiver-wire lottery ticket went off in Week 8. Asllani's only two games back and already sniffing blood in the water, which means this is exactly the week Muriqi's house of cards gets bulldozed by someone who actually made a coherent draft strategy. Time to find out if that 5-1 is legit or if it's just been luck cosplaying as competence.

Rinor's sitting at a pathetic 3-3 while these guys are cruising at 4-2, and honestly that gap feels generous—this week Rinor's going to find out what it's like when your waiver wire pickups actually show up to play instead of just taking up roster spots. Peter and Jetmir have figured out how to not completely sabotage themselves every Sunday, which is apparently a skill Rinor's still trying to learn.

Adam's sitting pretty at 2-4 like he's actually competing, but let's be real—you're one bad week away from free-falling into the basement where you belong. Rilind's already down there at 1-5, so at least this matchup gives one of you degenerates a chance to prove you're not completely hopeless, though honestly both your teams look like they were assembled by someone playing drunk at 3 AM.
